nnue.title: Engine strength (NNUE)
nnue.description: NNUE evaluates positions much more accurately than the classical evaluator. It needs a 40 MB file, downloaded once per device and then cached. Turn it off to skip that download on a metered connection, and analysis will use the weaker classical evaluator. Saved on this device.
nnue.applies: Takes effect the next time the engine starts.

workers.title: Engine workers
workers.description: How many Stockfish processes analyze a game at once. More is faster until memory runs out, then it gets much slower. Auto plays it safe because the browser can't tell how much memory is free. Raise it if analysis feels slow and you have RAM to spare, or lower it if the fans bother you. Saved on this device.
workers.applies: Takes effect on the next analysis.
workers.slowBuildTitle: Analysis is running ~11× slower than it should
workers.slowBuild: This page isn't cross-origin isolated, so Stockfish is using its single-threaded build. On the same game at depth 18 that takes 110 s instead of 9.7 s. The fast build needs the COOP and COEP headers from public/_headers. Check that they're deployed and that no proxy strips them.

freePlayStrength.title: Play vs engine: default strength
freePlayStrength.description: Used when you click "Play it out vs engine" after a practice line. Maximum is full-strength Stockfish. Lower levels weaken the engine so it plays more like a person. You can change it for a session on the practice page.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Chess Coach is a chess analysis tool that runs in your browser. In short: there is no Chess Coach server that stores your data, no analytics, no ad tracking, and no sharing with third parties.
privacy.localData: <bold>Locally in your browser (IndexedDB):</bold> the games you import, the engine evaluations Chess Coach computes for them, your repertoire trees, and which library puzzles you have solved. On most accounts this data stays on the device that created it. The puzzle library is a public dataset that ships with the app, so downloading it tells us nothing about you.
privacy.auth: <bold>Authentication:</bold> we use Clerk to sign you in. Clerk holds your email address and any OAuth identifiers (Google, GitHub) you choose to link. See <link>Clerk's privacy policy</link> for what they store about you.
privacy.profileSync: Profile sync (Supabase): we copy a small "profile row" (your Clerk user id and your Chess.com username) to Supabase so your devices can recognize the same account. Game data and analyses are not synced this way. They stay in IndexedDB on the device that created them.
privacy.cloudSync: Cloud sync (Supabase), off by default: for accounts where it's enabled, Chess Coach also copies imported games, their engine analyses and puzzle results to Supabase, so they survive a cleared browser and reach your other devices. It is not on unless the account has been added to an allowlist in the database, and the database rejects writes otherwise. When it's on, the Settings page shows a Cloud sync card with the last run and a button to sync manually. Nothing is shared with anyone else either way.
privacy.extSyncStorage: In chrome.storage.sync: your Chess.com username, the URL of your Chess Coach app, and a boolean toggle for whether to show the after-game prompt. Nothing else.
privacy.extSees: What the extension sees: only the URL and page content of chess.com tabs (by default it has no permission for any other site). When you click "Test connection" on the options page, it asks your permission to fetch the Chess Coach URL you set. That permission covers only that one site.
privacy.extSends: <bold>What the extension sends:</bold> nothing. The link it builds just opens a page in your own browser, so no data leaves your computer through the extension.
privacy.noAnalytics: No analytics, tracking pixels, or session-replay tools.
privacy.noSelling: No selling, renting, or sharing your information with third parties.
privacy.noChessReading: No reading of your chess.com account beyond the public game archive for the username you enter. Chess Coach uses Chess.com's public API and never asks for your password.
privacy.deleteDesc: Use Settings → Reset (or the browser's "Clear site data" devtool) to wipe IndexedDB. To remove the Supabase profile row, sign out of Clerk and email the address below. The extension's stored settings can be cleared by removing the extension from chrome://extensions.
privacy.contactDesc: Questions about this policy or about a deletion request: open an issue on the Chess Coach repository, or reach out via the email listed on the Chrome Web Store listing for this extension.

explain.missedMate: A forced mate was available here.
explain.allowedMate: This move allows a forced mate. Your opponent can now force checkmate.
explain.missedFork: A move was available that attacks two valuable pieces at once, so the opponent can't save both.
explain.missedPin: A piece could have been pinned against a more valuable one, freezing it in place.
explain.missedSkewer: A line attack on a valuable piece would have forced it to move, exposing the piece behind it.
explain.missedBackRank: The opponent's back rank was weak. A rook or queen could have mated, or threatened mate, on the back rank.
explain.fork: The opponent's reply attacks two of your pieces at once, and you can't save both.
explain.pin: Your piece is now pinned to a more valuable piece behind it, so it can't move without losing material.
explain.skewer: A line attack now forces a valuable piece of yours to move, losing the piece behind it.
explain.backRank: Your king is stuck on the back rank with no escape squares, so a rook or queen can mate it there.
explain.hangingPiece: A piece is left undefended, attacked by more pieces than defend it. The opponent can take it for free.
explain.trappedPiece: A piece has no safe squares left and will be lost next move.
explain.overloadedDefender: A defender has too many jobs. Covering one leaves another open.
explain.discoveredAttack: Moving one piece uncovers an attack from a piece behind it.
explain.weakKing: Your king has lost its pawn cover and several pieces are attacking it.
explain.lostMaterial: The line ends with you down material and nothing to show for it.
explain.other: A big drop in evaluation that doesn't fit a named tactic.

cloud.title: In the cloud
cloud.empty: Nothing uploaded yet. Run a sync.
cloud.hint: Only counts are read, a few hundred bytes each time. The numbers go up while the server analyzes your games, and refresh about once a minute until everything is analyzed with NNUE.

sync.title: Cloud sync
sync.description: Backs up your reviewed games, their engine analyses, and your puzzle progress to Supabase, so they survive a cleared browser and follow you to another device.
sync.archiveNote: The cloud copy only grows. Deleting a game here doesn't remove it from the cloud, and the next sync brings it back. To remove games from the backup, use the Supabase dashboard.
